title: EU AI Office Enforcement Powers (Articles 64–70): What GPAI Providers Need to Know — Council of AI Compliance Guide
context: 2026-08-31 autonomous EAT cycle — The EU AI Office, established under Article 64 of the AI Act, is the Union-level enforcement body for general-purpose AI (GPAI) models. It has direct investigative, corrective, and fining powers over GPAI providers regardless of where the provider is established. The Council of AI verified measurement credential provides the signed evidence stream GPAI providers need when the AI Office knocks.
body: The EU AI Office is not an advisory body. Under Articles 64–70 of the AI Act, it is the single most powerful AI regulator in the world — with direct enforcement powers over every general-purpose AI model placed on the EU market, regardless of where the provider is headquartered. Here is what every GPAI provider must understand. (1) Structure: The AI Office sits within the European Commission (Article 64). It is supported by a scientific panel of independent experts (Article 68) that can issue qualified alerts about systemic risks. If the scientific panel flags your model, the AI Office must investigate. (2) Powers: The AI Office can request documentation and information (Article 65), conduct evaluations of GPAI models including through adversarial testing (Article 66), request the market surveillance authority of a Member State to restrict or withdraw a model from the market (Article 67), and impose fines of up to 3% of annual worldwide turnover or €15 million for GPAI-specific infringements (Article 71). These powers are exercisable without a prior warning letter. (3) GPAI with systemic risk: Models trained with cumulative compute above 10^25 FLOPs are presumed to carry systemic risk and face enhanced obligations including model evaluations, adversarial testing, serious incident tracking, and cybersecurity protection (Article 55). The AI Office has sole enforcement competence for these models — national authorities cannot override its decisions. (4) The verified measurement answer: When the AI Office requests model evaluation evidence under Article 66, a GPAI provider can submit Council of AI board manifests — Ed25519-signed measurement records across 14 safety axes — as independently verifiable compliance evidence. Each manifest carries a body SHA-256 hash and a published public key; the AI Office can verify every reading without trusting the provider's word. The Council of AI Containment Index provides the serious incident tracking required by Article 55(1)(c) in a signed, append-only format. (5) Timeline: The AI Office became operational in February 2025. GPAI rules under Articles 52–55 apply from August 2026. The AI Office's first enforcement actions against GPAI providers with systemic risk are expected in Q4 2026–Q1 2027. Providers who maintain continuous measurement records from the Council of AI board position themselves as prepared — not panicked — when the letter arrives.
